record.paper_title: Models, feedback control, and open problems of 3D bipedal robotic walking
record.original_question: Develop models, analysis procedures, control designs, and especially stability notions for bipedal locomotion that do not assume the gait is periodic. In particular, characterize and control aperiodic walking behaviors that arise naturally when a biped walks over uneven ground or maneuvers around obstacles.

evidence.quote: The models, analysis procedures and control designs presented in the paper have focused on periodic locomotion. It is important to move beyond this assumption.
There is room for improved notions of stability of aperiodic walking gaits. Two cases where aperiodic gaits arise naturally are walking on uneven ground and maneuvering a biped around obstacles.

artifact.category_tag: Bipedal robotic walking / aperiodic gait stability
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a 3D bipedal walking robot modeled as a hybrid dynamical system

  Σ:  ẋ = f(x) + g(x)u   when x ∈ 𝒳 ∖ 𝒮,
        x⁺ = Δ(x⁻)        when x⁻ ∈ 𝒮,

where 𝒳 ⊂ ℝⁿ is the state manifold of joint positions and velocities, 𝒮 ⊂ 𝒳 is a switching surface representing foot impacts with the ground, Δ: 𝒮 → 𝒳 is a (possibly discontinuous) reset map encoding the impact dynamics and leg swap, and u ∈ ℝᵐ is the control input applied through joint actuators.

Most of the existing analysis and feedback-control framework for such systems (including hybrid zero dynamics and Poincaré-map-based stability analysis) assumes the closed-loop walking gait is a periodic orbit of Σ. The task is the following:

1. Define a precise and useful notion of stability for non-periodic (aperiodic) walking trajectories of Σ, applicable in particular to:
   (a) walking over terrain whose ground-height profile is not periodic and is not known in advance, and
   (b) maneuvering tasks where the biped must change heading and step placement to avoid obstacles, so that successive steps cannot be assumed identical.

2. Develop modeling, analysis procedures, and constructive feedback control designs that certify this stability notion for the hybrid system Σ in three spatial dimensions, without reducing the problem to tracking or stabilizing a predetermined periodic orbit.

Provide:
  - a formal definition of aperiodic-gait stability for Σ (e.g., in terms of forward invariance of a step-to-step set-valued map, input-to-state stability with respect to terrain/obstacle disturbances, or contraction of a non-autonomous Poincaré-like map);
  - analysis tools sufficient to certify this stability property;
  - a control synthesis methodology producing feedback laws u = k(x, ξ), with ξ encoding terrain/obstacle information, that achieve the stability property on a non-trivial class of 3D bipedal models.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a long-standing open research direction in legged locomotion control. While there has been substantial progress since 2014 on aperiodic and rough-terrain walking (e.g., step-to-step dynamics, control Lyapunov function and MPC-based approaches, capture-point/ALIP methods, and contraction-based analyses), no universally accepted stability notion or general control-design framework for aperiodic 3D bipedal gaits has emerged. The problem is generally regarded as still open.

status_evidence.title: Models, feedback control, and open problems of 3D bipedal robotic walking
status_evidence.snippet: Lists development of stability notions and control for aperiodic walking on uneven ground and around obstacles as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly posed as open in the source listing.

status_evidence.title: Survey of feedback control for bipedal walking (subsequent literature)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent surveys note that stability and control of non-periodic 3D bipedal gaits over uneven terrain remains an active research area without a unifying framework.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work treats aperiodic-gait stability as still under investigation.
